::: {.piege}
```{r}
ifelse(TRUE, as.Date("2026-10-22"), as.Date("2026-01-01"))
```
:::

## Why

`ifelse()` builds its result from the test, not from the values it returns. So it inherits the attributes of the test (none here) and loses those of the branches, including the `Date` class. What is left is the number of days since 1 January 1970. Factors suffer the same fate and become their integer codes.

## The fix

For a single condition, `if` is enough. For a vector, `dplyr::if_else()` and `data.table::fifelse()` keep the type and check that both branches are compatible.

::: {.piege packages="dplyr"}
```{r}
if (TRUE) {
  as.Date("2026-10-22")
} else {
  as.Date("2026-01-01")
}
dplyr::if_else(TRUE, true = as.Date("2026-10-22"), false = as.Date("2026-01-01"))
```
:::
